problem.title: Same Turn, Different Reach
problem.statement: Two ray pairs share a vertex. In each pair, one ray points east and the other points north. The first pair has rays 2 cm long; the second has rays 8 cm long. Which statement is true?
hints: East to north is one quarter of a full turn.

solutionSteps.title: Track the turn
solutionSteps.body: Both pairs turn from east to north, one quarter of a full rotation.

validationMethods: direction audit: both ordered ray directions are east and north
independent full-turn calculation: one quarter of 360° is 90°, making only choice C true

problem.title: Beside a Wide Angle
problem.statement: Two lines intersect. One angle measures 143°. What is the measure of an adjacent angle?
hints: Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180°.

problem.title: Clock Angle at Four
problem.statement: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at exactly 4:00?
hints: A clock has 12 equal gaps around 360°.
Count the smaller number of gaps from 4 to 12.

validationMethods: independent direction check: minute hand at 0° and hour hand at 120°; smaller separation 120°

problem.title: Carry, Then Complete
problem.statement: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle at the first intersection is 64°. The corresponding angle at the second intersection is adjacent to angle x. What is x?
hints: Corresponding angles are equal for parallel lines.

validationMethods: independent check: 64+116=180 and parallel condition is explicit; choice audit

problem.title: What Does the Sketch Prove?
problem.statement: A transversal crosses two lines that look parallel in a sketch, but no parallel marks or other relationships are given. One corresponding angle is 71°. What is the other corresponding angle?
hints: A sketch is not a stated relationship.
Ask what guarantees corresponding angles are equal.

solutionSteps.title: Check the condition
solutionSteps.body: Corresponding-angle equality requires the two lines to be parallel.

solutionSteps.title: Conclude
solutionSteps.body: Without that fact or another constraint, the second angle can vary and is not determined.

validationMethods: counterexample construction: rotate the second line while keeping the first crossing at 71°, changing the second angle
logical givens audit: no relation connects the line directions, so only choice D is guaranteed

problem.title: Interior Then Exterior
problem.statement: A triangle has two interior angles measuring 48° and 57°. What is the exterior angle adjacent to the third interior angle?
hints: First find the third interior angle.
The exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a straight line.

validationMethods: two-stage angle-sum calculation: third angle 75°, exterior 105°
